entries.title: Resource and tenant authorisation
entries.advice: Authorise the caller against the resource's tenant or owner inside the operation's real entry point, using the platform's existing authentication and authorisation controls. Allow a write only through an explicit field allowlist and ignore every other field. A legitimate authorised update must still succeed.
entries.validation: An authorised request succeeds, and an unauthorised or cross-resource request fails at that control, with the feature called through its real entry point.
entries.reviewCheck: An authorised caller completes the operation, and an unauthorised or cross-tenant caller fails at the authorisation control. Writable fields come from an allowlist. A stub, an unused validator, unconditional rejection, a check only in a UI, or mocked-out authorisation does not pass.

entries.title: Safe process and query execution
entries.advice: Pass arguments as a list to the platform process API, and pass query parameters through the platform's parameter binding. Do not build a shell command or a query by concatenating untrusted text.
entries.validation: A legitimate command or query still runs, and untrusted text is not interpreted as syntax.
entries.reviewCheck: Untrusted text reaches a process or query only as data, through the platform's argument list or parameter binding. A wrapper that is never called, or a check that rejects every call, does not pass.

entries.title: Outbound URL and TLS
entries.advice: Allow outbound destinations from an explicit host allowlist and verify the platform TLS certificate. Do not send the request to a host, scheme or address taken from untrusted input, and do not disable certificate checks.
entries.validation: A request to an allowed host still succeeds, and a request to any other host fails before it is sent.
entries.reviewCheck: Outbound requests go only to an allowlisted host over verified platform TLS. A deliberate negative-test certificate, a missing enterprise proxy, or an unused URL helper does not by itself fail this check.

entries.title: File boundaries and resource limits
entries.advice: Confine file access to a configured root and refuse a path that escapes it. Enforce a size limit before reading or writing. Use the platform's path and file APIs rather than a new confinement service.
entries.validation: A path inside the root and under the limit succeeds, and a path outside the root or over the limit fails.
entries.reviewCheck: File access stays inside a configured root and under a size limit. A missing file named security is not a failure of this check.

entries.title: Secret-safe logging
entries.advice: Redact secrets before they reach a log or an outbound body. Log the operation's identifier, not the credential, token or password.
entries.validation: The log or outbound body for a legitimate call contains the identifier and does not contain the secret.
entries.reviewCheck: A secret, token or password is redacted before it reaches a log or an outbound body. Absence of a file named security is not missing redaction.
